newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB to give extra support to Tokyo Leasing.
newsitem.headline: DKB to give extra support to Tokyo Leasing.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) said on Tuesday it would provide about 50 billion yen additional support to Tokyo Leasing Co Ltd, with which DKB has close ties.
DKB will provide the support by forgiving loans to the leasing firm. It will then sell the problem loans to the Cooperative Credit Purchasing Co Ltd (CCPC), it said in a statement.
CCPC is an organisation set up to rescue companies which are suffering from bad loans stemming from the bursting of the so-called bubble economy of inflated land prices.
DKB said the support would not affect the bank's earnings.
But it added that the support would be the last assistance Tokyo Leasing receives from the bank.

Tokyo Leasing began a three-year restructuring programme on March 31, but it recently asked DKB for additional support to tackle bad loans which have just emerged and because of a fall in prices of land offered as collateral, the bank said.
DKB said Tokyo Leasing's restructuring plan should be on track after the additional assistance.
Tokyo Leasing said earlier on Tuesday it posted a parent current profit of 1.63 billion yen in the six months to September 30, down 34.0 percent from the same period last year.
It expects a parent current profit of 3.3 billion yen for the full 1996/97 business year, down 4.1 percent from its actual parent current profit for the previous year.
